Disaffected

/dis-uh-FEK-tid/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Disaffected means rebellious, discontented, and disloyal toward those in authority.

After management broke its promise of safer equipment for the third time, the once loyal assembly crew grew openly disaffected, ignoring directives and talking of walking out.

Worked Example

The party had counted on the riverfront district for forty years, but its disaffected voters stayed home on election night. Years of ignored petitions and canceled town halls had drained away their old loyalty.

The voters have not merely lost enthusiasm; they have lost their loyalty to the party that once commanded it, which is what makes them disaffected rather than simply disappointed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rebellious: resisting authority or control

alienated: having lost connection or loyalty

discontented: dissatisfied with one's circumstances

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

loyal: faithful to an authority or cause

devoted: committed and dedicated

Where it sits · how far loyalty has broken down — dissatisfied → disaffected → mutinous

dissatisfied vs. disaffected: A dissatisfied employee grumbles about conditions, but a disaffected one has stopped feeling any loyalty to the employer at all.

mutinous vs. disaffected: Disaffected groups withhold loyalty and trust, while a mutinous group has moved beyond that into open revolt against its leaders.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: not, opposite of

Root — affect

Root — affect: to influence with feeling or loyalty

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Disaffected joins dis-, meaning not or opposite of, to the root affect, to influence or touch with feeling, plus the ending -ed. Someone disaffected has literally lost the loyal affection they once felt toward an authority or institution.

Use the root in a new word: affection

Use the root in a new word: affection: The old dog greeted every visitor with obvious affection, tail thumping against the floor.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / political and institutional

Disaffected is about lost loyalty, not just low spirits. It describes people, often groups, who have turned resentful and rebellious toward an authority such as a government, employer, or school. Unlike disheartened, which describes lost hope or morale after a setback, disaffected specifically implies that loyalty toward an institution has broken down.
